conventions: TypeScript monorepo (Yarn workspaces). Match the conventions of the file and package you are in; consistency inside a package beats consistency across the repo.
Every new .ts/.tsx file starts with the Apache 2.0 header exactly as in the stack profile, with 'Copyright 2026 The Backstage Authors'. Never touch the header year of an existing file.
Formatting is the repo Prettier config (single quotes, trailing commas, 2-space indent, 80 columns); the prettier fix runs before the check, so do not hand-align.

Imports: relative paths inside a package, '@backstage/*' package names across packages, 'node:' prefix for Node built-ins; keep the import grouping the file already uses; add no new package dependency to any package.json.
Never hand-edit anything under src/schema/openapi/generated/ in catalog-backend or catalog-client: those files come only from the tooling units that run the repo's OpenAPI generator.

Every new exported symbol gets a TSDoc block and a release tag: '@public' in catalog-model, catalog-client and catalog-node public API; existing translation refs keep their current tag. Internal helpers get no release tag.
UI strings come from the package's translation ref via useTranslationRef (catalogTranslationRef in plugins/catalog, techdocsTranslationRef in plugins/techdocs); no hard-coded English in components.

Tests are Jest, co-located '*.test.ts(x)' files, nested describe + it, fewer thorough cases with several expect calls each. React tests use React Testing Library with screen and findBy* queries, no test IDs, and waitFor only where the file already relies on it for hooks.
Do not change any existing public signature; new interface members are optional where the decisions say so.
Docs follow docs/contribute/doc-style-guide.md: sentence-case headings, short paragraphs, second person, YAML examples in fenced blocks, no marketing words.
Changesets are hand-written '.changeset/<kebab-name>.md' files with a YAML front matter of package names to bump types, then a plain-language adopter-facing message; never edit an existing changeset.

decisions.topic: Annotation constant and parsing helper names (catalog-model)
decisions.choice: Constant ANNOTATION_FORMER_NAMES = 'backstage.io/former-names' in src/entity/constants.ts; helper getEntityFormerRefs(entity: Entity): string[] in new file src/entity/formerNames.ts, exported from src/entity/index.ts, both @public.
decisions.reason: The helper needs the entity for kind/namespace defaults and self-ref removal, and constants.ts is where generic metadata annotations live.

decisions.choice: An entry is parsed with parseEntityRef(entry, { defaultKind: entity.kind, defaultNamespace: entity.metadata.namespace || DEFAULT_NAMESPACE }); it is skipped when parsing throws or when any of kind, namespace or name contains ':', '/' or whitespace; results are stringifyEntityRef output (lower-cased), deduplicated in first-seen order, and the entity's own ref is dropped.
decisions.reason: FR-2 requires never throwing and normalized refs; parseEntityRef alone accepts 'a:b/c/d' as name 'c/d', which is not a valid ref.

decisions.topic: Search row key for former refs
decisions.choice: One row per former ref under key 'former_entity_ref' (constant FORMER_ENTITY_REF_SEARCH_KEY exported from plugins/catalog-backend/src/database/operations/stitcher/buildEntitySearch.ts), pushed only when the ref length is at most MAX_VALUE_LENGTH (200).
rejected: reusing key 'metadata.annotations.backstage.io/former-names' with one row per entry
decisions.reason: Entity.schema.json forbids extra top-level properties, so a dot-free key outside apiVersion/kind/metadata/spec/relations/status can never collide with a real field path, and no migration is allowed.

decisions.choice: GET /entities/by-former-name/{kind}/{namespace}/{name}, operationId GetEntityByFormerName (generated client method getEntityByFormerName), 200 returns the Entity schema, every miss returns 404 through writeSingleEntityResponse with the message `No current entity found for former entity ref '<ref>'` where <ref> is the stringified requested ref.
rejected: a query flag on the by-name endpoint
decisions.reason: A separate path keeps the by-name route untouched (FR-9) and avoids clashing with the by-name sub-resource routes.

decisions.topic: Backend resolver shape and permission split
decisions.choice: EntitiesCatalog.resolveFormerEntityRef(request: ResolveFormerEntityRefRequest): Promise<EntitiesBatchResponse> with request { formerEntityRef, filter?, fields?, credentials }. DefaultEntitiesCatalog runs the real-name check and the claimant count without any filter, then reads the single claimant through this.entitiesBatch with request.filter. AuthorizedEntitiesCatalog applies catalog.entity.read exactly like its entitiesBatch (DENY gives one null item without delegating, CONDITIONAL delegates with the permission predicate as filter, ALLOW delegates unchanged).
rejected: returning only the target ref and reading it in the router
decisions.reason: FR-6/FR-7 must ignore permissions while FR-8 must apply them, and reusing the entitiesBatch permission pattern keeps one tested code path for reads.

decisions.choice: Three indexed queries plus the entitiesBatch read: final_entities by entity_ref (real-name check), search by key and value selecting distinct entity_id with limit 2 (claimants), final_entities by entity_id (target ref). No query against final_entity JSON and no full scans.
decisions.reason: NFR-4 asks for a small fixed number of indexed queries; limit 2 is enough to detect a conflict.

decisions.choice: Optional member getEntityByFormerRef?(entityRef: string | CompoundEntityRef, options?: CatalogRequestOptions): Promise<Entity | undefined> on CatalogApi; CatalogClient, InMemoryCatalogClient and both mocks implement it; callers guard with catalogApi.getEntityByFormerRef before calling.
decisions.reason: FR-11/NFR-3: existing CatalogApi implementers must compile unchanged.

decisions.choice: CatalogService mirrors CatalogApi, so it gains optional getEntityByFormerRef?(entityRef, options: CatalogServiceRequestOptions); DefaultCatalogService implements it and returns undefined when the wrapped CatalogApi lacks the method; CatalogServiceMock and catalogServiceMock.mock list it.
decisions.reason: FR-13 applies wherever the interface mirrors CatalogApi, and it does.

decisions.choice: On a hit, the page calls navigate(newUrl, { replace: true, state: { formerEntityRef } }) where formerEntityRef is stringifyEntityRef of the URL's kind/namespace/name and newUrl is the current entity's base route plus the sub-path after the old base route, plus location.search and location.hash. The notice components read formerEntityRef from useLocation().state; dismissing only hides the notice (local state).
decisions.reason: History state survives the replace, never shows on a freshly opened URL, and keeps the visible URL clean.

decisions.choice: New component EntityRenamedNotice (plugins/catalog/src/components/CatalogEntityPage/EntityRenamedNotice.tsx) rendering '@material-ui/lab/Alert' severity 'info' with onClose and closeText from translations, used by both the old CatalogEntityPage and the alpha CatalogEntityPage directly inside AsyncEntityProvider before the layout.
decisions.reason: Both systems already funnel through useEntityFromUrl and the two CatalogEntityPage components, so two small edits cover FR-18.

decisions.choice: TechDocsRedirectNotification gains an optional actionLabel prop (defaults to the existing 'Redirect now' text); new internal component TechDocsRenamedNotice renders it with the renamed message, actionLabel 'Dismiss', a no-op handleButtonClick and autoHideDuration 15000; TechDocsReaderPage renders it in both return branches. The alpha reader page reuses TechDocsReaderPage through TechDocsReaderRouter, so no alpha edit is needed.
decisions.reason: FR-20 asks to reuse the existing redirect-notice component.

units.behaviour: Parses an entity's backstage.io/former-names annotation into a deduplicated list of normalized, fully-qualified former entity refs, never throwing.
rules: 1. Start with the 2026 Apache header. Import DEFAULT_NAMESPACE and ANNOTATION_FORMER_NAMES from './constants', parseEntityRef and stringifyEntityRef from './ref', and the Entity type from './Entity'.
2. Read the value with optional chaining: entity.metadata?.annotations?.[ANNOTATION_FORMER_NAMES]; if it is not a string, return [].
3. Compute the entity's own ref once with stringifyEntityRef({ kind: entity.kind, namespace: entity.metadata.namespace || DEFAULT_NAMESPACE, name: entity.metadata.name }).
4. Split the value on ',', trim each entry, and skip empty entries.
5. Parse each entry with parseEntityRef(entry, { defaultKind: entity.kind, defaultNamespace: entity.metadata.namespace || DEFAULT_NAMESPACE }) inside try/catch; a thrown error skips the entry.
6. Skip the entry when any of the parsed kind, namespace or name contains ':', '/' or whitespace (test with one regex such as /[:/\s]/).
7. Normalize with stringifyEntityRef(parsed); skip it when it equals the own ref or was already returned; otherwise append it, keeping first-seen order.

8. TSDoc on the exported function: summary line, a '@remarks' paragraph describing the comma-separated format, the short-ref defaults, and that malformed entries, duplicates and the entity's own ref are dropped; '@public', '@param entity - The entity to read the annotation from', '@returns A list of lower-cased, fully-qualified entity refs'.

units.behaviour: Implements resolveFormerEntityRef with the real-name-wins and single-claimant rules over indexed final_entities and search rows, then reads the claimant through entitiesBatch with the request filter.
rules: 1. Add ResolveFormerEntityRefRequest to the '../catalog/types' import and import FORMER_ENTITY_REF_SEARCH_KEY from '../database/operations/stitcher/buildEntitySearch'.
2. Add `async resolveFormerEntityRef(request: ResolveFormerEntityRefRequest): Promise<EntitiesBatchResponse>` right after entitiesBatch.
3. Define the miss result once as { items: { type: 'object', entities: [null] } } and return it for every miss.
4. Real-name check, ignoring request.filter: query final_entities where entity_ref equals request.formerEntityRef, select entity_id, limit 1; if a row exists return the miss.

5. Claimant check, ignoring request.filter: query search where key equals FORMER_ENTITY_REF_SEARCH_KEY and value equals request.formerEntityRef, select distinct entity_id, limit 2; if the row count is not exactly 1 return the miss.
6. Look up final_entities by that entity_id selecting entity_ref; if there is no row or no entity_ref return the miss.
7. Return this.entitiesBatch({ entityRefs: [thatRef], filter: request.filter, fields: request.fields, credentials: request.credentials }).

8. Never log anything in this method (no names, refs or counts of claimants); use typed knex calls (this.database<DbFinalEntitiesRow>('final_entities'), this.database<DbSearchRow>('search')) like the rest of the file.

rules: 1. Imports: add stringifyEntityRef from '@backstage/catalog-model', useRouteRef from '@backstage/core-plugin-api', entityRouteParams from '@backstage/plugin-catalog-react', and useLocation from 'react-router-dom'; keep the existing imports.
2. Add const location = useLocation() and const entityRoute = useRouteRef(entityRouteRef) next to the existing hooks.

3. The useAsyncRetry callback becomes async: const entity = await catalogApi.getEntityByRef({ kind, namespace, name }); if entity is set or catalogApi.getEntityByFormerRef is missing, return { entity, renamedTo: undefined }; errors from getEntityByRef still propagate.

4. Otherwise call catalogApi.getEntityByFormerRef({ kind, namespace, name }) once, treat a rejection as undefined, and return { entity: undefined, renamedTo }. Keep the dependency list [catalogApi, kind, namespace, name].

5. Add a useEffect on the result: when value?.renamedTo is set, compute oldBase = entityRoute({ kind, namespace, name }), newBase = entityRoute(entityRouteParams(value.renamedTo)), rest = location.pathname.startsWith(oldBase) ? location.pathname.slice(oldBase.length) : '', then navigate(`${newBase}${rest}${location.search}${location.hash}`, { replace: true, state: { formerEntityRef: stringifyEntityRef({ kind, namespace, name }) } }).
6. Keep the existing no-name useEffect unchanged.

7. Return { entity: value?.entity, loading: loading || Boolean(value?.renamedTo), error, refresh } so the page never shows 'Entity not found' while redirecting; on a miss the result is exactly today's (entity undefined, loading false).

units.behaviour: Documents the backstage.io/former-names annotation: format, short-ref defaults, the real-name and conflict rules, permissions and when it takes effect.
rules: 1. New section `### backstage.io/former-names` between the view-url/edit-url section and the source-location section, shaped like its neighbours: a fenced yaml '# Example:' block, then prose.
2. The example shows metadata.name 'new-name' with `backstage.io/former-names: old-name, legacy-team/older-name, component:other/renamed-service`.

3. Prose covers: the value is a comma-separated list of entity refs; a short ref takes the entity's own kind, and its own namespace when none is given; malformed entries are ignored; when someone opens the old catalog entity page or TechDocs URL, Backstage redirects to the entity's current page and shows a notice.

4. A short list of rules: an entity that currently has the old ref is always served instead of redirecting; when several entities declare the same former ref, no redirect happens; the redirect only happens for users allowed to read the current entity, and otherwise they see the usual not-found page; API calls by entity name are not redirected.

5. End with a sentence that the annotation takes effect once the catalog has processed the entity again, and link the endpoint section of the API docs ([catalog API](api.md#get-entitiesby-former-namekindnamespacename)).
